findings.source_passage: the sun still low and only touching the hilltops and shining far to seaward
findings.why_it_matters: This lyrical environmental detail is part of Stevenson's distinctive scene-painting prose; the draft compresses the January morning description and cuts the sun imagery entirely, flattening the atmospheric voice-establishing passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sun detail: 'the sun still low and only touching the hilltops and shining far to seaward' within the morning description.

findings.source_passage: a most horrible change came over his tallowy face, and he ordered me in with an oath that made me jump. As soon as I was back again he returned to his former manner
findings.source_locator: paragraph 8, Black Dog calling Jim back from road
findings.why_it_matters: The grotesque shift in Black Dog's manner — the 'horrible change' in his tallowy face — is interpretively important for characterising him as genuinely dangerous beneath the fawning, and the specific phrasing is stylistically distinctive. The draft merely says 'he called me back with an oath.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'horrible change came over his tallowy face' and the return to fawning manner — this two-beat characterisation of Black Dog is signature.

findings.source_passage: "I have a son of my own," said he, "as like you as two blocks, and he's all the pride of my 'art. But the great thing for boys is discipline, sonny--discipline. Now, if you had sailed along of Bill, you wouldn't have stood there to be spoke to twice--not you. That was never Bill's way, nor the way of sich as sailed with him."
findings.source_locator: paragraph 8, Black Dog's speech about discipline
findings.why_it_matters: The 'pride of my 'art' phrasing and the full cadence of the discipline speech — 'not you. That was never Bill's way' — is stylistically distinctive dialect writing. The draft cuts 'not you' and 'he's all the pride of my 'art,' losing the grotesque pathos that makes the passage memorable.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'he's all the pride of my 'art' and 'not you. That was never Bill's way' to preserve the full voice of this speech.

findings.source_locator: paragraph 6, Black Dog's speech about the cut on the cheek
findings.why_it_matters: The cryptic 'Ah, well! I told you' — spoken apparently to himself — is a small but tonally distinctive moment of menace and self-satisfaction that the draft drops without replacement.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Ah, well! I told you.' in Black Dog's speech about the cheek.

findings.source_passage: It was tattooed in several places. "Here's luck," "A fair wind," and "Billy Bones his fancy," were very neatly and clearly executed on the forearm
findings.source_locator: paragraph after Dr. Livesey arrives, tattoo description
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'very neatly and clearly executed' and 'on the forearm' is dropped; 'were on it' replaces this. Minor compression but the precision of 'neatly and clearly executed' is part of Jim's observational voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'very neatly and clearly executed on the forearm' rather than the bare 'were on it.'

summary: The draft is largely faithful and preserves the chapter's major set-pieces and signature dialogue verbatim, but suffers from several medium-grade voice flattenings — most notably the compressed January morning description, the erasure of Black Dog's 'horrible change' of face, and the trimmed discipline speech — none individually severe enough to trigger regeneration.
